footer.label: Footer
footer.blurb: openplate is an open-source food diary, built in Berlin. The app and the sync server are MIT licensed.

hero.body: openplate is an open-source food diary that runs on your device, with an optional photo scan that estimates the macros on your plate. It is for people who want to track what they eat without sending their diary to someone else's server.
hero.lead: openplate is for people who want to track what they eat without sending their data to someone else's server.
hero.inviteNote: Sign up on the hosted instance at app.openplate.de without an invitation, or run your own copy at no cost.
hero.shotAlt: The openplate diary for one day on a computer screen. Net carbs are logged against the daily limit. Calories, protein, fat, and fiber are shown against their targets. The day's food splits into carbs, fiber, protein, and fat.
hero.researchBadge: We are looking for research partners

features.heading: What you can do with openplate

add.title: Log a food
add.body: Search the food database, or pick something you logged before, and the entry lands in the day under the meal you chose.
add.alt: The add-food screen: a search box, your usual dinner, a button to scan a plate, and recently logged foods with their net carbs.

scan.title: Scan a plate
scan.body: Photograph the plate and the AI service you connected estimates the carbs. The photo goes to that service and to nowhere else.
scan.alt: The scan screen, offering to connect an AI provider before it reads a photo, and a way to log the food without one.

goals.title: Choose how you eat
goals.body: Low-carb, calories, high protein, or simple tracking. The style you pick sets which goal grades the day, and every goal is optional.
goals.alt: The eating and targets screen: eating style options, from low-carb to simple tracking, and preset daily carb limits.

overview.title: See where the day stands
overview.body: Net carbs, calories, protein, fat, and fiber for the day, each shown against its target, and how many of the last seven days you logged.
overview.alt: The overview screen: the day's net carbs, calories, protein, fat, and fiber, each displayed with a bar against its target.

flow.label: Five boxes and five arrows. The app server sends the page to your device. Your device sends the diary to openplate-core, encrypted. Your device sends the plate photo to the AI endpoint you chose. Your device sends food names to the app server, which passes them on to the food database. The app server is on neither the diary path nor the photo path.

holders.caption: The drawing shows what each one stores. The table adds what each one sees while your data passes through it.

stack.heading: Three components, each optional beyond the app
stack.intro: The app works on its own to keep a diary. The sync server and inference runtime add features. Both are separate programs that you can run yourself or leave out entirely.

analytics.heading: What we measure
analytics.body: openplate records nothing until an operator turns tracking on. The hosted instance at openplate.de counts page visits and which features get used. It is never told what you eat, weigh, or log. Anyone running their own copy picks one of three levels, from page visits only up to a research level that records health behaviour for a study with consenting participants. No third party sits in the path. The numbers land in a Matomo instance we run ourselves, with cookies switched off. <configuration>Configuration</configuration> lists every event at every level.

access.heading: Getting access
access.body: Anyone can sign up on the hosted instance at app.openplate.de without an invitation. The diary, the account and sync are free. Plate scanning and the other AI features come with a paid plan, after a free three-day trial. Running your own copy costs nothing. See <selfHosting>Self-hosting</selfHosting>.

openSource.heading: Open source
openSource.body: openplate and openplate-core are MIT licensed. openplate-inference carries its own terms, set by the model weights it ships; its licensing guide lists them. Read the code, change it, run it yourself: <repoApp>github.com/LowCarbCheck/openplate</repoApp>, <repoSync>github.com/LowCarbCheck/openplate-core</repoSync>, <repoInference>github.com/LowCarbCheck/openplate-inference</repoInference>.

why.heading: Why openplate exists
why.body: Most food trackers store your diary on their servers, where you cannot control it. openplate works the other way around. Your diary stays on your device. The source code is public, so anyone can inspect it. Every additional service, sync and photo scanning included, is optional, and you can host each part yourself.

research.heading: Research partners
research.body: We are looking for universities, nutrition researchers and clinical teams who want to work with openplate. A diary stored on the participant's device, code an ethics board can inspect, and research analytics that record only with consent make it a practical base for dietary studies.

app.title: The app
app.lead: openplate logs food and, if you want it, estimates the macros on a plate from a photo. Search a food or scan a plate, and the entry lands in your diary for the day. On your own install, there is no sign-up screen: open the app and start logging. On the hosted instance, you sign in first.
app.shotIntro: The diary is one day at a time: the meals you logged, what they cost against the day's limit, and what is left of it.
app.shotAlt: The openplate diary on a phone. Net carbs are logged against the daily limit. Calories, protein, fat, and fiber are shown against their targets.

stores.heading: What it stores on the device

core.title: The sync server
core.lead: openplate-core carries your diary between your devices. It stores an email address and an encrypted copy of your diary. It also keeps your recovery code, sealed under a secret of its own, so a forgotten password returns your diary. That same code lets the operator of an instance open a diary on it.

reads.heading: What it can and cannot read

inference.title: The inference runtime
inference.lead: openplate-inference is a plate-photo scanner you run on your own hardware. It names the foods on a plate and estimates the grams, then looks up the macros in a bundled food database rather than inventing numbers.

audience.heading: Who it is for
audience.body: Self-hosters who want plate scans with no cloud AI account and no photo leaving their network. It is not part of the hosted instance at openplate.de.

deploy.title: How to run openplate
deploy.lead: You can use openplate without running anything at all, and you can run every part of it yourself. Four rungs sit between those two. Each rung adds a capability and adds something you now have to operate, so read it as a ladder you are meant to stop climbing early.

rung0.heading: Use an instance someone else runs

rung1.heading: Run the app on your own box

docs.title: Documentation
docs.intro: These pages document all three services: the app, the sync server, and the self-hosted inference runtime. Start with the service you are running, or with Self-hosting if you are starting from nothing.

pricing.title: Pricing
pricing.heading: Plans
pricing.vatNote: Every price is a final price in euros, German VAT included.
pricing.trial: A new account on the hosted instance gets a free three-day trial. After the trial, plate scanning pauses until a plan is bought, and the rest keeps working.
pricing.intro: openplate is free to use. A plan pays for plate scanning and the other AI features on the hosted instance at app.openplate.de.

selfHost.name: Self-host
selfHost.body: Run openplate on your own server. Every feature is included, you connect your own AI provider, and you pay us nothing.

monthly.name: Monthly
monthly.body: Renews each month until you cancel. A cancellation takes effect at the end of the paid month.

yearly.name: Yearly
yearly.body: Paid in advance for one year. A cancellation during the year takes effect at its end. After the year it continues as the monthly plan, cancellable every month, and never renews for another year.

pricing.includes: openplate Plus includes plate scanning and the other AI features, up to 200 AI requests a day.
pricing.free: Without a plan, the diary, the account and sync across devices stay free.

research.title: Research
research.heading: openplate for research
research.lead: We are looking for research partners: university groups, nutrition researchers, dietitians and public health teams who study dietary intake. openplate is an open-source food diary that runs on the participant's device, and we want it to serve research as well as daily logging.

open.title: Open code
open.body: The app and sync server are published under the MIT licence. An ethics board or data protection officer can inspect how the software handles data instead of relying on vendor descriptions.

device.title: The diary stays on the device
device.body: A participant's diary stays on their own phone or computer. Sync is optional and encrypted. Studies can host the sync server on their own institution's infrastructure.

consent.title: Consent comes first
consent.body: The analytics have a research level that records health behaviour for a study with consenting participants. It stays off until the instance operator turns it on.

photo.title: Logging from photos
photo.body: Participants can log meals by photographing their plate. Image estimates can run through a cloud model or through openplate-inference on hardware your institution controls.

base.title: A base to build on
base.body: Deploy an instance on your institution's infrastructure and adapt it to your protocol. There are no licence fees and no vendor contracts.

custom.title: Study-specific builds
custom.body: We configure openplate for your protocol, including custom dietary targets, questions, food databases and languages.

export.title: Data export with consent
export.body: Participants share diary records with the study only after granting consent. We structure exports to match your analysis pipeline.

grants.title: Joint grants and papers
grants.body: We are looking for co-applicants on grant proposals and for joint publications, for example on image-based dietary assessment.

seek.heading: Who we are looking for
seek.nutrition: University groups in nutrition science, medicine and public health
seek.clinical: Dietitians and clinical teams running intervention studies
seek.hci: Researchers in human-computer interaction who study self-tracking
seek.vision: Groups working on food recognition and portion estimation from images

write.title: Write to us
write.body: Tell us about your group, your research questions and your timeline.

call.title: Initial call
call.body: We discuss your protocol, what openplate supports now, and what adjustments your study needs.

scope.title: Written scope
scope.body: Before any work begins, we agree in writing on the deliverables, data handling procedures and result ownership.

contact.heading: Get in touch
contact.body: Email <email>{{email}}</email>. A short summary is enough: your team, your research focus, and what your study requires from openplate.
